02 / 21

Meet Lata

Start with one home.

Lata lives in a village with her family. Her husband farms. Some months are steady, some are not.

Her children's needs depend on what the household can manage that season. Her life does not fit into one neat category.

03 / 21

When one thing begins to slip

Lata's husband has been coughing for weeks. Then the cough gets worse.

He misses two days in the field.
The sowing is delayed.
Money kept aside for seeds goes into travel and medicines.
The children's school expenses are pushed back.
Meals become simpler for a few weeks.
Lata takes on more work, but has less say in what gets cut first.
Nothing looks like a crisis on day one.
By the end of the month, one health problem has become an income problem, a farming problem, a nutrition problem, and an education problem.
04 / 21

One problem rarely stays as one problem

A health expense can disturb the whole household.
A weak crop can affect what the children need.
If income slips, nutrition slips.
If Lata is not part of decisions, many choices stay smaller than they need to be.
05 / 21

This is rural life

Everything is connected to everything else.

06 / 21

The LHWRF insight

LHWRF works where health, livelihoods, agriculture, women's participation, and community systems meet.

The family is bigger than one home

In a village, support has many faces.

08 / 21

Health protects the family

Care protects more than health.

For Lata's family, healthcare access does not only mean treatment. It means less fear of sudden shocks.

A screening, a diagnosis, a follow-up, or timely care can protect income, time, confidence, and household stability.

09 / 21

Livelihoods give the family room to plan

Income changes the horizon.

For Lata's family, livelihood support does not only mean more income. It means more room to plan.

When farming support, livestock, skills, or market access improve, the family can think beyond the next crisis.

10 / 21

Women change the direction of the household

When Lata has more say, the family has more ways forward.

Her participation can affect savings, nutrition, enterprise, health awareness, children's needs, and the confidence to try something new.

Women's agency is not a side story. It is central to the family's progress.

Community helps change last

Progress becomes stronger when it is not carried alone.

12 / 21

This is The Family Of Change

No single intervention creates rural transformation.

Change lasts when many forms of support come together around a family. That is the story LHWRF is already living on the ground.

13 / 21

The communication shift

From: "LHWRF conducted a program."
To: "Here is what became stronger around Lata's family."

This moves LHWRF from isolated activity updates to connected impact communication.

15 / 21

Why this can hold the communication together

LHWRF has many stories to tell: farmer progress, healthcare access, women's participation, field teams, community institutions, regional voices, and partnerships.

The Family Of Change gives all of them one centre.

16 / 21

Closing thought

This is not only Lata's story.

It is about many women and families like Lata's, and the many forms of support that come together until a family can move forward. And when many families move forward, the village begins to change too.

That is the role LHWRF can become known for.

Social media direction

How The Family Of Change shapes the social media presence

It gives every piece of communication a way to show the full picture of rural development.

A story can begin with a woman, a farmer group, a health camp, a village meeting, a milestone, or a moment of celebration.

Together, these pieces show the conditions that help rural families and communities move forward.

Platform roles

One idea, three platform roles

The idea stays the same. Each platform helps build a different kind of connection.

Instagram

Goal: Make the work visible, human, and easy to engage with.

It can carry field moments, reels, carousels, explainers, topicals, achievements, and community celebrations in a way that keeps the organisation present in everyday feeds.

ReelsCarouselsField momentsTopicals
f

Facebook

Goal: Build regional familiarity and community connection.

It can carry village updates, local-language posts, event albums, programme activities, community celebrations, field participation, and regional stories that help the work feel closer to the geographies it serves.

Regional storiesAlbumsLocal updatesCommunity moments
in

LinkedIn

Goal: Build credibility, partnerships, and participation.

It can carry impact proof, programme thinking, leadership notes, milestones, awards, media mentions, event participation, careers, and collaboration calls.
